On April 1, 2025, an attacker exploited UPCX's ProxyAdmin contract on Ethereum to upgrade core protocol logic with a malicious withdrawByAdmin function, draining $70 million (18.4 million UPC tokens) from protocol management wallets. No user wallets were affected. A single privileged ProxyAdmin key was compromised, permitting an instant malicious contract upgrade. The new implementation exposed a drain primitive (withdrawByAdmin) with no access control or delay, allowing the attacker to withdraw all UPC tokens from protocol management accounts. No multisig or timelock was enforced, leaving the protocol vulnerable to single-point takeover.
